text:
I want agent sessions, build sessions especially, to show rich visualizations in the chat: flow diagrams, maps of the parts a change touches, and so on, drawn with our own design system's components. Propose a decision for how this fits the architecture. Discuss it with me before writing anything.

My starting position:

The agent never writes HTML into the chat. Its words go through renderMarkdown, which escapes raw HTML (server/views.js), and the views part is responsible for that safety. A visual is data in a small, versioned vocabulary, for example a fenced block. Prelude parses it, checks it (part ids must exist), and renders a design-system partial from it. Anything it can't parse stays a plain code block.
The vocabulary reuses what the architecture already defines: a flow's steps (1. <part id>: <text>), and parts and their layers for the map.
Some visuals need no agent at all. After a build or fix turn, the architecture check already maps the changed files to parts, so Prelude could show those parts on a map by itself.
Not web components. Koda keeps custom elements for host-owned renderers of negotiated media types (node_modules/@kodalang/core/docs/reference.md, "A renderer that is a native component"), which is too heavy for something inside a transcript entry.
Decide with me:

which part parses and renders visuals (views, or a new part);
how the vocabulary is versioned, and how agents are told it (agent.js);
where it happens in the turn flow (flows/turn.md): at save time or at render time.
Before proposing, check how Koda's renderMarkdown handles a fenced block's language tag, since that decides whether blocks are pulled out before rendering or after. Then write the proposed decision, any new or changed part, and a flow "A visual in a message".

"Ask and fix conversations use the same transcript (_session.eta → _chat → _entry). Note that askPrompt gets no architecture brief today, and decide whether it should, since an ask is where 'how does this work' gets answered. The vocabulary goes into askPrompt and fixPrompt too.

3061	### What is not known
3062	
3063	Which hops happened. A response says only that it *was* redirected, so `302` and
3064	`303` - which turn a `POST` into a `GET` - cannot be told apart from `307` and
3065	`308`, which preserve the method. Koda treats any redirect as "the result is at
3066	this URL", which is what the first pair mean.
3067	
3068	So a `307` or `308` answering a `POST` into a region that owns history would
3069	record a URL that only answers `POST`. Use `303` for post-redirect-get, which is
3070	what it is for.
3071	
3072	## Markdown
3073	
3074	`renderMarkdown(source, options)` returns `{ html, headings }`. It is pure and
3075	lives in `src/core`, so it is tested as string assertions with no DOM.
3076	
3077	Supported: ATX headings, paragraphs, fenced code with a language class, inline
3078	code, bold, italic, links, images, ordered and unordered lists with wrapped
3079	continuation lines, tables with alignment, horizontal rules and blockquotes.
3080	Everything else is escaped and passed through, so an unsupported construct is
3081	visible rather than silently dropped.
3082	
3083	Code spans are extracted before any other inline processing and restored last,
3084	so backticked content is never reinterpreted as emphasis, a link, or markup.
3085	
3086	A link or image keeps its URL only if it is relative or uses a safe scheme:
3087	`http`, `https` or `mailto` for a link, `http` or `https` for an image. Anything
3088	else - `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:` - is left as the text it was written
3089	as, so markdown from anyone can be rendered into a region without putting a
3090	script on the page.
3091	
3092	`headings` is `{ level, text, id, line }` per heading: its slug, and its index in
3093	the source. That is enough to build a table of contents, or to split the source
3094	into sections, without parsing anything again, which is what the docs site and
3095	its search do. A repeated heading's slug is numbered (`notes`, `notes-1`).

1	# Prelude architecture
2	
3	Prelude is a tool for designing and then building an app with an agent: you pick a project, chat with the Claude Code CLI, and watch the design appear beside the chat. It runs as one Node server (plain `node:http`, views in Eta, Koda in the page) on localhost:4200, optionally inside a Tauri desktop window. Everything it produces is files in the project's `prelude/` folder, each design worked on in its own git branch and worktree. Agent-written views render in a sandboxed child process, and each design is served on its own preview origin.
4	
5	## Layers
6	
7	1. Windows
8	2. Entry points
9	3. Pages
10	4. Agent and live state
11	5. Designs and hosting
12	6. Project files
13	7. Shared helpers
14	8. Outside
15	
16	## Principles
17	
18	- **The folder is the database.** Everything Prelude makes is a file under the project's `prelude/`, committed with the code; `~/.prelude/` holds only machine-local conveniences, so nothing is lost if it's deleted.
19	- **The server is the single source of truth for live state.** Every window (chat, pop-out, browser tab) renders from the server and re-renders on its SSE events, so no window holds state another needs.
20	- **Agent-written code never runs in the server's process.** A design's views render in a sandboxed renderer, and a host that runs them unsandboxed starts only once the person approves it.
21	- **The agent works with ordinary file tools, fenced to what it may touch.** It reads the project and the folders added as references, writes only where its mode allows, and deletes by writing a file empty.
22	- **A design's memory is its files, not a conversation.** Each session starts from NOTES.md, the views and states, so sessions on different machines and branches pick up where the work stands.
23	- **Committed files must merge cleanly.** Session folders and decision ids are random, transcripts are append-only, and there's no shared index that every session rewrites.

I've read the code and haven't written anything yet. Here's what I'd propose.

## What Koda's `renderMarkdown` does with a fence

`src/core/markdown.js:77`: `FENCE = /^```\s*([A-Za-z0-9_-]*)\s*$/`. A fence block always becomes `<pre><code class="language-x">` with its body escaped, and there's no way to hook into that. Three things follow from this:

- **The version has to be part of the tag.** The tag allows only letters, digits, `_` and `-`, and nothing can come after it. A fence written as `flow v1` or `flow@1` doesn't match, so that line renders as a paragraph. Then the closing ```` ``` ```` opens a new code block that swallows the rest of the message. So the tag has to look like `prelude-flow-1`.
- **Blocks have to be pulled out before rendering.** Doing it afterwards would mean matching `class="language-…"` in Koda's HTML and un-escaping the body, which ties us to its output.
- **Pulling them out first is safe.** Paragraphs, lists, tables and quotes all end at a fence line. So if we split on top-level fences using the same regex, and the same `^```` rule for closing, and render the pieces in between separately, the HTML comes out the same. A fence inside a `>` quote isn't top-level, so it stays a code block. A fence still streaming in without its closing line stays a code block until it closes.

## Proposals

**1. A new part, `visuals`, in Shared helpers (`server/visuals.js`, no uses).** It splits a message, parses each block and checks it, and holds the vocabulary's text for prompts. `views` uses it and renders the parsed model with partials (`_flow.eta`, plus a `_map.eta` taken out of `architecture/overview.eta:48`, so the Architecture page and the chat draw the same map). It has to sit in Shared helpers because `agent` (Agent and live state) imports the vocabulary text, and `views` is a layer above that. `architecture` would also use its step parser, so a flow file and a flow block are read by one function. `views` stays responsible for safety: escaping, plus one rule: a block that fails stays a code block.

**2. The vocabulary, version 1:**
- ```` ```prelude-flow-1 ```` is an optional `# title`, then `1. <part id>: <text>` steps, exactly like `flows/*.md`.
- ```` ```prelude-map-1 ```` is one `<part id>` per line, optionally followed by `: <note>`. It draws the whole map with those parts highlighted.

A block that names a part that doesn't exist, or doesn't parse, stays a code block.

Versioning works like this:
- Adding something optional doesn't change the version.
- A breaking change gets a new tag (`-2`).
- Prelude keeps rendering every version it has ever shipped, because transcripts are committed and append-only.

Agents are only told the current version: `visuals.js` exports the brief, and `agent.js` appends it to the build, fix and ask prompts when the project has an architecture. Without one there's nothing to check ids against.

**3. Words are saved as written and interpreted when shown; facts are saved when they happen.**
- **Agent visuals are handled when shown.** The transcript keeps the agent's text unchanged, so it merges cleanly and reads fine as a code block on GitHub. `presentEntry` parses it, and the ids are checked against the architecture of the session's branch as it is now. If a part gets renamed later, an old block falls back to code, which is honest. `server` passes the parts and layers in the present context that both `main.js` and `turns` already take.
- **The automatic map is saved at save time.** After a build or fix turn, `checkAfterTurn` already maps the changed files to parts. `turns` records a `{ type: 'parts', ids, files }` entry, because which files a turn changed can't be recovered cheaply later. That entry is then rendered like the agent's maps.

**4. `askPrompt` should get an architecture brief, but a read-only one.** The current `architectureBrief` is about changing code ("before you change anything", "propose a decision"), which doesn't fit an ask. I'd add a short variant:
- read the overview and the parts the question touches;
- answer in terms of parts, citing their files;
- in "what you'd change", name the parts it reaches and say whether it would need a decision.

An ask reads main's architecture. When the conversation moves on to a fix branch, the same transcript is checked against that branch's architecture.

## Questions for you

1. When a block names a part that doesn't exist, should the agent be told with its next message, like drift is? I'd say no for now: the code-block fallback is enough.
2. Should design sessions get the vocabulary too, or only build, fix and ask?
3. Are you happy with the tag names `prelude-flow-1` and `prelude-map-1`?

Once you've confirmed, I'll write the decision (proposed), the `visuals` part, the changes to `views`, `agent`, `architecture`, `turns` and `flows/turn.md`, the flow "A visual in a message", and the notes.

2	status: proposed

6	## Context
7	Every prompt points the agent at Prelude's own installed Koda (`server/main.js` resolves `@kodalang/core`), so an app on another version gets guidance for attributes it doesn't have. Upgrading an app's Koda needs `npm install`, which the agent can't run and nothing in Prelude does. `node_modules` isn't in git, so a fresh worktree has none, and merging an upgrade leaves the old Koda installed in the person's checkout.
8	
9	## Decision
10	`designs` finds the app's Koda and reads its version from `node_modules/@kodalang/core/package.json`: first in the worktree (the app's path from `prelude.json`, then the root), then the same in the project's own checkout, and Prelude's only when neither has one. It also reads the version the app's `package.json` asks for. The server passes the Koda it found to every prompt as `kodaPath` and to `--add-dir`, and the design host serves its runtime to a design's pages (`/_prelude/koda/`), so designs behave as the app will; Prelude's own pages keep Prelude's.
11	
12	`pages` compares the app's version with Prelude's on the project page and offers an upgrade, which starts a fix. A new part, `installs`, runs the project's package manager (chosen by its lockfile) in two places: in that fix's worktree, installing Prelude's version, and in the person's checkout once the upgrade is merged, installing the version `package.json` asks for. `pages` offers that second install when the checkout's installed Koda isn't the one it asks for. Either way the command is fixed (never one the agent wrote), names only `@kodalang/core`, has a time limit, and runs only after the person approves it, seeing it first, as with a host: install scripts are code from outside the project.

I've written it up as a proposed decision, D-v3x, with your three answers built in.

**Adding new visuals:** the new `visuals` part (`server/visuals.js`, in Shared helpers) keeps a list of visual kinds. For each kind it has:
- a parser for every version that has ever shipped;
- the check against the architecture's parts;
- the lines that describe the current version to the agent.

A visual is a fenced block tagged `prelude-<kind>-<version>`. To add one, you add an entry to that list and a `_visual-<kind>.eta` partial in `views`. That entry's lines then reach every prompt automatically.

**New files:**
- `decisions/D-v3x.md`: the decision, including why the version goes in the tag. Koda's fence pattern accepts only `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` and nothing after the tag, and it offers no hook for fenced blocks.
- `parts/visuals.md`
- `flows/visual.md`: "A visual in a message", from the prompt to the partial.

**Changed files:**
- `views`: now uses `visuals`. It takes the blocks out before `renderMarkdown` runs and renders them with the partials. Anything that fails to parse or check stays a code block, and the agent isn't told. The map partial is shared with the Architecture page.
- `agent`: now uses `visuals`. Design, build, fix and ask prompts all get the vocabulary once the project has an architecture. Ask also gets a read-only architecture brief.
- `architecture`: now uses `visuals`, because the flow-step parser is shared. It also names the parts that a turn's changed files belong to.
- `turns`: records those parts as an entry, which the chat draws as a map.
- `flows/turn.md`: steps 3, 5 and 9 are updated, and step 11 is new: the visuals are drawn when an entry is shown.
- `NOTES.md`: both decisions are added.

Until a build session writes the code, the check will report `server/visuals.js` as missing. It will also report that the new `uses` don't match the imports yet.
